Looking to acquire a "moderately priced" vehicle for hauling stuff and generally fuckery. Any of you ever been to an auto auction (not the fancy kind) and what are your experiences?

I bought a couple cars from auctions. As long as you are just looking for cheap cars, under a few thousand dollars, and you can turn wrench, I think this is the best way to get a deal. If your looking for a nicer car it's a little tougher, because the dealer's(both the used car and drug types), will outbid you. All cars are As-Is,so you can get a lemon,but most auctions don't do anything to hide problems so you know what you are getting.For under a thousand bucks you can get a descent go to work car, you may not want to drive it on the express way, and you might have to put some new tires on it,used tires are cheap at a junkyard, and nobody will be impressed with how it looks.

I don't mind auction cars. Just make sure you leave room in the budget to make some repairs. You will almost always have at least one needed repair. If you're budget is $2k, don't spend more than $1300 on a car.

Also, as with any auction, know what you are willing to pay and do not exceed it or enter into a bidding war.

As stated by the other poster, especially don't enter a duel with a dealer. They likely have resources (financial and repair) that you don't. A $1300 car to you might mean a $1550 car for them...if that makes sense.

Thanks. That makes sense about the dealers too. I am really looking for a cheap-o vehicle (some minor repairs are not a big deal as I am somewhat handy) that I can haul some stuff with and generally not care too terribly much about damaging it. Appreciate the response/advice. Cheers!
